lead: Arcarine (development code ORM-11984) is an investigational selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) developed by the Finnish drugmaker Orion Corporation. SARMs are designed to switch on the androgen receptor in tissues such as muscle and bone more than in tissues such as the prostate, which is why the class is of interest to people who want more muscle and a more muscular physique.[1][2][1]

Orion studied Arcarine for benign prostatic hyperplasia, hypogonadism and osteoporosis, with the intended benefit of anabolic effects in muscle and bone and less androgenic activity elsewhere.[2] It reached Phase I clinical trials and development was then discontinued; its chemical structure has not been disclosed.[1][2] No human efficacy results have been published.

The wider SARM class has a looks-related profile: bodybuilders and athletes use SARMs for muscle gain, and trials of the best-studied SARM, enobosarm, have reported increased lean body mass, with weaker evidence for improved strength or function.[1] Arcarine itself is not described as a product sold on the gray market.

chain: Compound designed to activate androgen receptors in muscle and bone
Potentially more lean mass and a more muscular look
angle.text: As a SARM, Arcarine was designed to act on muscle and bone, which is the mechanism behind interest in the class for physique building. For Arcarine specifically, only early development exists and the muscle effect in humans has not been reported.

paras: Orion Corporation developed Arcarine as a candidate for benign prostatic hyperplasia, hypogonadism and osteoporosis, aiming for anabolic effects in muscle and bone with less activity in tissues such as the prostate.[2] Wikipedia lists it among candidates that reached Phase I and were then discontinued; a drug database listed the research programme in November 2017.[1][2] The reasons for discontinuation have not been stated.

The first nonsteroidal SARMs were developed in 1998 and the term was introduced in 1999 by analogy with selective estrogen receptor modulators.[1] Proposed reasons for tissue selectivity include that SARMs are not converted by 5-alpha-reductase to the more potent DHT and that tissues differ in coactivator and corepressor levels.[1] SARMs have been studied for osteoporosis, muscle wasting, benign prostatic hyperplasia, stress urinary incontinence, breast cancer and hypogonadism.[1]

Several trials showed increased lean mass, while evidence of improved strength or physical function has been weaker and regulators have not accepted lean mass alone as sufficient.[1] As of 2023 neither the FDA nor the EMA had approved any SARM.[1]

No studies found in humans. Arcarine reached Phase I only. A 2015 rat study in Acta Orthopaedica tested local delivery of ORM-11984 from a polymer implant in a bone marrow ablation model and found a negative correlation between dose and new bone around the implant, with only a mild, non-significant increase at the lowest dose.[3] A 2022 review covered SARMs developed for osteoporosis from 1998 to 2021.[2]

The World Anti-Doping Agency has banned SARMs since 2008, and one study found most products advertised as SARMs on internet gray markets were mislabelled.[1] Reported adverse effects of the class include elevated liver enzymes and case reports of liver injury, lower HDL cholesterol and dose-dependent suppression of the hormonal axis.[1]

timeline.event: Rat study reports local ORM-11984 delivery did not work as a bone anabolic agent.[3]
AdisInsight lists the Arcarine research programme.[2]

card.summary: Orion's discontinued SARM candidate; reached Phase I and left almost no public data on muscle or looks.
card.note: Investigational only; never approved, with no published human efficacy data.

quick.overview:
Arcarine (ORM-11984) is a selective androgen receptor modulator that Orion Corporation developed for conditions such as benign prostatic hyperplasia, hypogonadism and osteoporosis.

It reached Phase I trials before development was discontinued. It is not a marketed product, and no human data on muscle or appearance outcomes have been published.
quick.mechanism: As a SARM, it was designed to activate androgen receptors in tissues like muscle and bone while having weaker effects on the prostate. Its structure was never disclosed, and a rat study of local delivery reported it did not act as an anabolic agent in that model.
quick.risks: No safety data are published. SARMs as a class are unapproved, banned by WADA, and have been linked in case reports to liver injury with recreational use.
